styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small, roughly 1x2-tile prop. Its measured facts sit in the range of the simple Beodeul props: 13 colours per full tile against 10 for the hedge and 17-20 for the stall and well, and 13 distinct colours against 11-14 for the hedge, bench and lamp. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat areas. Only 15% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline leans dark red-brown next to the red body and brown next to the base, not a black sticker line. By eye, the red cabinet has about 4 lightness steps (highlight, mid, shadow, dark). The gold trim, the reel window with its red and white symbols, and the base add dot-level variation, so the surface is not flat. It has fewer steps than the 5-6 on the stall roof or well, and less grain than they carry, which is why density is slightly lower. For a small single-material-group prop it is still comparable to the hedge and bench, and a careful artist would accept it next to them without it looking sticker-like.
